newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds tread water before data.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds tread water before data.

text.p: *Australian bonds treading water ahead of release of key labour force data on Thursday, slightly easier after U.S. Treasuries soften on refunding auctions.
*Positive fundamentals expected to support bonds in face of any renewed U.S. weakness.

Australian bonds were treading water as they awaited the release of July labour force data on Thursday, ending SYCOM trading flat to slightly weaker after U.S. Treasuries eased on the first day of quarterly refunding.

The extra Treasury supply, combined with some concerns that the U.S. Federal Reserve may have to lift rates in August or September in the face of stronger economic data, meant the market had a slightly heavy feel about it, traders said.
While the U.S. will have an impact on the local market, the market's focus is Thursday's jobs data, which is expected to confirm the labour market remained soft going into 1997/98.
Positive local fundamentals are expected to keep the local market supported in the face of any U.S. weakness, with the potential for the spread to Treasuries to narrow further.

"Until the market is convinced that rates have bottomed for this cycle, growth indicators start picking up solidly and the labour market shows convincing signs of life, the spread may narrow further," Hambros said in a bond market outlook.
The Reserve Bank of Australia held its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, but given last Wednesday's cut in official interest rates, no announcement is expected this morning.
